rows.source_population: bilingual adult-child family caregivers of older Hmong American parents managing type 2 diabetes mellitus at home in Wisconsin
rows.family_population: adult child carer describing a 74-year-old mother on daily metformin with 3 days of excessive urination and a home blood sugar monitor reading of 580 mg per dL
rows.note: Same adult-child caregiver / older diabetic mother home-monitoring context; verbatim caregiver phrase 'blood sugar monitor' used directly.

rows.source_population: adults with symptomatic cholelithiasis interviewed in hepatobiliary surgery after delayed care-seeking prior to acute hospital presentation (quote from Respondent P13, aged 58)
rows.family_population: 51-year-old adult with dark brown skin having postprandial right-subcostal aches after greasy food and new scleral yellowing today
rows.note: Same middle-aged symptomatic gallstone / biliary disease population experiencing postprandial flare-ups before acute hospital presentation; verbatim patient phrase 'after eating greasy food' used directly.

rows.source_population: adults with symptomatic cholelithiasis interviewed in hepatobiliary surgery after delayed care-seeking prior to acute hospital presentation (quote from Respondent P13, aged 58)

rows.note: Same middle-aged symptomatic biliary disease population attributing postprandial symptoms to benign indigestion; verbatim quote 'I had just thought it was indigestion and hadn’t taken it seriously.' adapted into present-tense belief clause 'and I think it's indigestion'.

rows.source_population: adults diagnosed with temporomandibular disorder interviewed on bruxism, jaw symptoms, and pain expression (quote from Patient 7)

rows.note: Same adult temporomandibular disorder and nocturnal clenching population; verbatim patient phrase 'wake up clenching my teeth' used directly.

rows.source_population: adults diagnosed with temporomandibular disorder interviewed on jaw symptoms and coping (quote from Patient 4)
rows.family_population: adult with 4 months of morning sore back teeth, waking up clenching teeth, and jaw joint clicking and catching on wide mouth opening
rows.note: Same adult temporomandibular disorder population; verbatim patient symptom term 'clicking' used in 'jaw joint clicking and catching'.

rows.source_population: adults diagnosed with temporomandibular disorder interviewed on perceived symptom triggers (quote from Patient 6)
rows.family_population: adult with 4 months of morning sore back teeth, waking up clenching teeth, and jaw joint clicking and catching on wide mouth opening
rows.note: Same adult temporomandibular disorder population attributing symptoms to life stress; verbatim quote 'Maybe there was stress in my life.' adapted into present-tense belief clause 'and I think it's stress'.

rows.source_population: older adults living with Parkinson disease interviewed in Sweden regarding physical symptom barriers including hand tremor and shaking

rows.note: Same older-adult parkinsonism / resting-hand-tremor population; authors' report of participant symptom wording 'shaking' used verbatim.

rows.source_population: married couples who experienced infertility and underwent IVF in Uganda interviewed on delayed conception (summary referring to 49-year-old male participant James)
rows.family_population: 28-year-old woman trying to conceive through regular intercourse with her 29-year-old husband for 18 months
rows.note: Same couple-infertility domain seeking fertility care ('trying for a baby' used verbatim), adapted from an authors' summary of a 49-year-old male IVF spouse to a 28-year-old female spouse with 18 months of primary subfertility.

rows.family_population: 28-year-old woman trying to conceive through regular intercourse with her 29-year-old husband for 18 months
rows.note: Same couple-infertility pre-diagnosis causal attribution ('We thought maybe the timing was off or stress.'), adapted from a 45-year-old male spouse with secondary infertility to a 28-year-old female spouse's belief clause 'and I think our timing was off'.

rows.source_population: 37-year-old male electrician presenting with 2 months of recurrent occupational lateral elbow pain related to repetitive gripping and pulling at work (Patient 2 in 2-patient lateral elbow tendinopathy case report)
rows.family_population: 44-year-old carpenter using hand tools daily with 4 weeks of sharp outer right elbow pain when gripping tools
rows.note: Same adult manual-trades occupational lateral elbow tendinopathy presentation provoked by repetitive work gripping; 'gripping' used verbatim.

rows.source_population: adult patient in Veraval, Gujarat, India reporting acute symptoms including giddiness and vertigo after consuming cooked pufferfish (case report)
rows.family_population: 29-year-old Indian English speaker on daily blood pressure tablets with 1 hour of mild giddiness this morning and a home cuff reading of 224 over 128
rows.note: Same Indian English clinical domain where the patient explicitly reported 'giddiness' (used verbatim, matching core entry 'giddiness / feeling giddy' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json), adapted from an acute pufferfish poisoning presentation in Gujarat, India to acute symptomatic severe hypertension on home blood-pressure monitoring.

rows.source_population: adult patients referred for syncope-spectrum complaints ('falling out', 'passing out', 'fainting') at the Nashville, Tennessee Veterans Administration Hospital
rows.family_population: 54-year-old US dialect English speaker with 5 months of recurrent brief orthostatic syncope ('falling out') on standing despite 6 weeks of doctor-prescribed compression stockings
rows.note: Same adult US clinical syncope-referral population using referral complaint 'falling out' verbatim in the medical syncope sense (matching core entry 'fell out / falling out' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json).

rows.source_population: Indian English speakers using 'loose motion' / 'loose motions' for diarrhea (Wiktionary lexical entry 'loose motion', Noun sense 1; attests regional lexical sense)
rows.family_population: 32-year-old Indian English speaker experiencing daily diarrhea ('loose motions') and mild abdominal bloating after drinking milk for 4 weeks
rows.note: Wiktionary Indian English dictionary sense ('Diarrhea', labeled 'India, sometimes in the plural', matching core entry 'loose motions' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json) attests regional lexical meaning rather than a chronic post-milk diarrhea outpatient cohort.

rows.source_population: English speakers using adjective 'short-winded' for breathlessness (Wiktionary lexical entry 'short-winded', Adjective sense 1; attests lexical sense only)
rows.family_population: 64-year-old adult developing 3 weeks of new exertional breathlessness ('gotten short winded') walking up steep hills after an indoor winter
rows.note: Wiktionary dictionary sense ('Out of breath, gasping for air... or given to becoming short of breath', matching core entry 'short winded' in dialect_lexicon_20261109.json) attests general lexical meaning rather than an older-adult exertional dyspnea primary-care cohort; written unhyphenated as 'short winded'.
